# Shroom Labs

> Shroom Labs is a library of researched mushroom grow profiles. Apply them from a Hub to a chamber running OpenShrooly.

Site: https://shroomlabs.io
Full text for every guide and profile: https://shroomlabs.io/llms-full.txt

All numbers on this site come from the published grow profiles. Temperatures are in °C with °F in brackets.

## Start here

- [Mushroom growing conditions for every species](https://shroomlabs.io/grow): one table with fruiting temperature, humidity, light, and days for each species.
- [How to grow mushrooms at home](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/grow-mushrooms-at-home): The easiest way to grow mushrooms at home is to start with an oyster or lion's mane kit or a colonized block, keep it at 85 to 95% humidity with regular fresh air, give it indirect light, and keep the room cool. Most kits start forming mushrooms one to two weeks after you open them. When that works, a fruiting chamber makes every grow repeatable.
- [What is the easiest mushroom to grow at home?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/easiest-mushrooms-to-grow): Oyster mushrooms are the easiest mushroom to grow at home. Pearl and blue oyster colonize fast, shrug off small mistakes, and run about 29 and 25 days in their profiles from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window. Lion's mane is a close second and just as good in a kit.
- [Grow kit vs monotub vs smart chamber](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/grow-kit-vs-monotub-vs-smart-chamber): A grow kit is the cheapest and simplest way to get a first harvest. A monotub gives bigger harvests from bulk substrate but takes more hands on work and clean technique. A smart fruiting chamber holds humidity, fresh air, and light for you, and some also manage temperature, so results repeat, but it costs more up front.
- [How much humidity and fresh air do mushrooms need?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/humidity-and-fresh-air): Most culinary mushrooms need 86 to 95% humidity while pins form and 82 to 93% while they fruit, plus regular fresh air to clear the carbon dioxide they breathe out. Too little humidity gives dry, cracked caps and stalled pins. Too little fresh air gives long stems and small caps. The two pull against each other, so the goal is steady humidity with gentle, regular air changes.
- [Why are my mushrooms not pinning?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushrooms-not-pinning): Mushrooms usually fail to pin for one of two reasons: the block is not fully colonized yet, or nothing has told it to fruit. Pins form when the block is fully white and then gets a change: cooler air, more fresh air, higher humidity, and light. Check those four, give it a week, and most blocks start to pin.
- [Why do my mushrooms have long stems and small caps?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/leggy-mushroom-stems): Long, thin stems with small caps almost always mean too much carbon dioxide. The mushrooms are stretching to reach fresh air. Add more air changes, open more holes, or fan more often. If air is good, check light next: mushrooms in a dark corner also stretch toward the nearest light.
- [Why are my mushroom caps dry or cracked?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/dry-cracked-mushroom-caps): Dry, cracked, or curled caps mean the mushrooms are losing water faster than the block can supply it. Usually the air is drier than the species wants, or a fan, heater, or vent is blowing straight on them. Raise humidity, block direct airflow, and keep air changes gentle. Most culinary profiles here fruit at 82 to 93% humidity.
- [Is my mushroom block contaminated?](https://shroomlabs.io/guides/mushroom-contamination): Healthy mycelium is white, sometimes with yellow or amber drops. Contamination usually shows as color: green, blue-green, black, pink, or orange patches, or wet, slimy spots that smell sour. If you see colored mold, bag the block, take it outside without opening it, and clean the area. Do not eat mushrooms from a moldy block.

## Grow guides by species

- [How to grow Beech / Buna Shimeji](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/beech-shimeji): To grow Beech / Buna Shimeji at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 40 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Blue Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/blue-oyster): To grow Blue Oyster at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 14 °C (57 °F) and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 25 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Button / Cremini](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/button-cremini): To grow Button / Cremini at home, colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and no light. This profile runs about 36 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Chestnut Mushroom](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/chestnut): To grow Chestnut Mushroom at home, colonize at 23 °C (73 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 92% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 34 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Cordyceps militaris](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/cordyceps-militaris): To grow Cordyceps militaris at home, colonize at 20 °C (68 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 18 °C (64 °F) and 84% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 57 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Elm Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/elm-oyster): To grow Elm Oyster at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 31 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Enoki](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/enoki): To grow Enoki at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 93% humidity with little fresh air and no light. This profile runs about 43 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Golden Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-oyster): To grow Golden Oyster at home, colonize at 25 °C (77 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 21 °C (70 °F) and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 24 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow King Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster): To grow King Oyster at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 15 °C (59 °F) and 82% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 38 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow King Oyster: thick-stem method](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster-thick-stem): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 43 days from start to fruit.
- [How to grow Lion's Mane](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/lions-mane): To grow Lion's Mane at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 17 °C (63 °F) and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 33 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Maitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/maitake): To grow Maitake at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 54 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Nameko](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/nameko): To grow Nameko at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 14 °C (57 °F) and 93% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 39 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Pearl Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pearl-oyster): To grow Pearl Oyster at home, colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 29 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Pink Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pink-oyster): To grow Pink Oyster at home, colonize at 27 °C (81 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 24 °C (75 °F) and 86% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 20 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Pioppino](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pioppino): To grow Pioppino at home, colonize at 25 °C (77 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 31 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Reishi](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/reishi): To grow Reishi at home, colonize at 27 °C (81 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 23 °C (73 °F) and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 77 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Shiitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/shiitake): To grow Shiitake at home, colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 16 °C (61 °F) and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 74 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Turkey Tail](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/turkey-tail): To grow Turkey Tail at home, colonize at 24 °C (75 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 20 °C (68 °F) and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 78 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Wine Cap](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wine-cap): To grow Wine Cap at home, colonize at 22 °C (72 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 17 °C (63 °F) and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 40 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
- [How to grow Wood Ear](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wood-ear): To grow Wood Ear at home, colonize at 26 °C (79 °F) in the dark, then fruit at 24 °C (75 °F) and 92% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h of light a day. This profile runs about 38 days from the start of colonization to the end of the first harvest window.
